## Final Submission: data cleaning

```{r}

#clean maternal vitamin D measurements
#the original values have text before the measurement
#so remove everything before the colon, then convert the values
#to numeric, so vitamin D concentrations can be continuous.
covarData <- covarData |>  
  mutate(mat_vitD = as.numeric(str_remove(mat_vitD, ".*:"))
         )

#confirm that vitamin D is numeric
#class(covarData$mat_vitD)
#summarize the data to check if everything is reasonable
#summary(covarData$mat_vitD)

#create a categorical vitamin D variable from the continuous
#measurement so that individuals with levels < 30ng/ml are
#insufficient and >= 30ng/ml are sufficient
covarData <- covarData |>  
  mutate( 
    vitData = if_else(mat_vitD >= 30, "Sufficient", "Insufficient")
  ) 

#count the individuals in each vitamin D group
#table(covarData$vitData)

#rename first column of the gene expression set
#contains microarray probe IDs but imported as "X" so renaming
#it to match it to the gene names set.
geneexpressionData <- geneexpressionData |>  
  rename(PROBEID = X)

#turn the gene expression data to long format
#long format puts all sample IDs into one column and 
#expression values in another so each row can represent 1
#probe measurement for 1 sample. 
#PROBEID column unchanged, need to match with the genes
geneexpressionLong <- geneexpressionData |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -PROBEID, 
    names_to = "geoID", 
    values_to = "expression"
  )

#check to see if the gene names set has duplicate probe IDs
#which could make more rows when merging sets
#sum(duplicated(genenamesData$PROBEID))

#look at the original pregnancy outcome categories
#to see how normal pregnancy and preeclampsia are recorded
#table(covarData$preg_preeclampsia)

#clean the pregnancy outcome labels
#remove "pregnancy_condition:"
#makes it much simpler for boxplot
covarData <- covarData |>  
  mutate(preg_preeclampsia = str_remove(preg_preeclampsia,
                                        "pregnancy_condition: "))
#confirm that everything is correct and
#count individuals for normal / preeclampsia
#table(covarData$preg_preeclampsia)

#merge all three data sets
#match gene expression measurements to gene names
#using PROBEID, then match those to maternal
#characteristics using geoID, then it should 
#result in a data set that gives you gene expression
#+ gene name + participant info all together
mergeData <- geneexpressionLong |>  
  left_join(genenamesData, by = "PROBEID") |>  
  left_join(covarData, by = "geoID")

#look at merged data and check dimensions / 
#first few rows
#dim(mergeData)
#head(mergeData)

```

## Final Submission: visualization functions

```{r}
#plot 1: histogram of gene expression
#describes how expression is distributed across the sample, with 
#the x axis showing expression values and the y showing participant n.
#looking at most common expression values / overall shape 

#function allows same histogram to be made for different genes
#data is the data frame and gene finds which gene to plot
histoPlot <- function(data, gene) {
  
#filter data to keep observations for the selected gene
plotData <- data |>  
  filter(GENE == gene)
  
ggplot(plotData, aes(x = expression)) + 
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.1, 
    fill = "#377EB8",
    color = "black"
  ) + 
  #automatically update title and x axis for each gene (functions are cool) 
  #& so are italicized names
  labs( 
    x = bquote(italic(.(gene)) ~~ "Expression"),
    y = "Number of Participants"
  ) +
  #keep it all the same across all plots
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_rect(
      color = "gray40",
      fill = NA, 
      linewidth = 0.5
      ), 
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 10,
      margin = margin(t = 12)
      ),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 10,
      margin = margin(r = 12)
    ),
plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
) 
} 

#histoPlot(geneData, "SGK1")
#histoPlot(geneData, "FOSL1")
#histoPlot(geneData, "FOSL2")
```


```{r}

#plot 2: scatterplot of maternal vitamin D and gene expression
#describes the relationship between vitamin D concentration and
#expression for each gene, with both variables being continuous. 
#each point is one individual's vitamin D concentration and gene expression.

#function allows same plot to be made for different genes, continuous 
#says which variable to use on x axis 
scatterPlot <- function(data, gene, continuous) {

#filter data to keep observations for specific gene
plotData <- data |> 
  filter(GENE == gene)

#use continuous variable in the function
#compare with expression for the gene
ggplot(plotData, aes(x = .data[[continuous]], y = expression)) + 
  geom_point(
    color = "#377EB8",
    size = 2, 
    alpha = 0.7
  ) + 
   #label axes and italicize gene names
  labs( 
    x = "Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)",
    y = bquote(italic(.(gene)) ~~ "Expression")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_rect(
      color = "gray40",
      fill = NA, 
      linewidth = 0.5
    ), 
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 10,
      margin = margin(t = 12)
      ),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 10,
      margin = margin(r = 12)
    ),
plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
) 
}

#scatterPlot(geneData, "SGK1", "mat_vitD")
#scatterPlot(geneData, "FOSL1", "mat_vitD")
#scatterPlot(geneData, "FOSL2", "mat_vitD")
```


```{r}

#plot3: boxplot of gene expression by pregnancy outcome and vitamin D status. 
#compares gene expression across two categorical variables
#pregnancy outcome places individuals into normal and
#preeclampsia groups. Vitamin D status places individuals
#into sufficient and insufficient groups. 
#each box summarizes the distribution of expression within a group.

#function allows same plot to be made for different genes
#categorical finds two variables used to group people
boxPlot <- function(data, gene, categorical) {
  
#filter to keep observations for the specific gene
plotData <- data |>  
  filter(GENE == gene)

#first categorical determines x axis
#second determines fill colors
#expression compared by resulting groups
ggplot(plotData, aes(x = .data[[categorical[1]]], 
                     y = expression, 
                     fill = .data[[categorical[2]]]
  )) + 
  geom_boxplot(
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.8, 
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) + 
  #adding jitter per submission 1 correction
    geom_point(
    position = position_jitterdodge(
      jitter.width = 0.25, 
      dodge.width = 0.75
    ),
    size = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.5, 
    color = "black"
  ) +
  #use same colors for vitamin D across all
  #box plots
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Insufficient" = "#377EB8",
               "Sufficient" = "#E15759")
    #label axes and italicize gene names
  ) + 
  labs( 
    x = "Pregnancy Outcome",
    y = bquote(italic(.(gene)) ~~ "Expression"),
    fill = "Vitamin D Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_rect(
      color = "gray40",
      fill = NA, 
      linewidth = 0.5
    ), 
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 10,
      margin = margin(t = 12)
      ),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 10,
      margin = margin(r = 12)
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
  )
}

#boxPlot(geneData, "SGK1", c("preg_preeclampsia", "vitData"))
#boxPlot(geneData, "FOSL1", c("preg_preeclampsia", "vitData"))
#boxPlot(geneData, "FOSL2", c("preg_preeclampsia", "vitData"))
```

## Final Submission: plots

```{r}
#the main function to plot all three types for selected genes
#takes a data frame, gene names, and one continuous
#covariate, and two categorical covariates
plotGenes <- function(data, genes, continuous, categorical) {
  
  #loop through each gene 
  for(gene in genes) {
    
    #histogram of expression distribution
    print(histoPlot(data, gene))
    
    #scatterplot comparing expression with 
    #selected continuous covariate
    print(scatterPlot(data, gene, continuous)) 
    
    #boxplot comparing expression across two
    #categorical covariates
    print(boxPlot(data, gene, categorical))
  }
}

#run the function using SGK1, FOSL1, FOSL2
#maternal vitamin D is the continuous covariate
#pregnancy outcome and vitamin D status are
#categorical
plotGenes(
  data = geneData, 
  genes = c("SGK1", "FOSL1", "FOSL2"),
  continuous = "mat_vitD",
  categorical = c("preg_preeclampsia", "vitData")
) 

```

## Final Submission: summary stats and table 1

```{r}
#head(covarData$mat_age_yrs)
#head(covarData$delivery_gestAge_wks)

#converting maternal and gestational age to numeric 
#remove text before the colon so can get summary stats 
coolTable <- covarData |> 
  mutate(
    mat_age_yrs = as.numeric(str_remove(mat_age_yrs, ".*:")), 
    delivery_gestAge_wks = as.numeric(str_remove(delivery_gestAge_wks, ".*:"))
  )

#Check distribution of the continuous variables
#using histograms 
hist(coolTable$mat_age_yrs)
hist(coolTable$delivery_gestAge_wks)
hist(coolTable$mat_vitD)

#calculate median and IQR for each continuous
#variable and separate by pregnancy outcome
coolTable |>
  group_by(preg_preeclampsia) |>  
  summarize(
    across( 
      c(mat_age_yrs, delivery_gestAge_wks, mat_vitD),
    ~ paste0(
      round(median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 2), " [",
      round(quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 2), ", ",
      round(quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "]"
    )
  )
 ) 

#count vitamin D status by pregnancy outcome to get n and % 
coolTable |>  
  count(preg_preeclampsia, vitData) |>  
  group_by(preg_preeclampsia) |>  
  mutate(percent = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))

#count maternal asthma by pregnancy outcome to get n and %
coolTable |>  
  count(preg_preeclampsia, mat_asthma) |>  
  group_by(preg_preeclampsia) |>
```

## Final Submission: heatmap

```{r}
#select 10 genes from the merged data for the 
#heatmap
hotinHere <- mergeData |>  
  filter(GENE %in% c(
    "SGK1", "FOSL1", "FOSL2",
    "TRIM24", "HSPA8", "SLC1A5", 
    "RBL2", "AQP9", "TGFB1I1", "GRB2"
  ))

#View(hotinHere)
#unique(hotinHere$GENE)

#reshape from long to wide so each row
#is a gene and each column is a person
#values = gene expression
wideHeat <- hotinHere |>  
  select(GENE, geoID, expression) |>  
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = geoID,
    values_from = expression
  )

#head(wideHeat)

#convert wide data into matrix because
#pheatmap needs a matrix
keanuReeves <- wideHeat |>
  column_to_rownames("GENE") |>  
  as.matrix()

#View(keanuReeves)

#create the annotation data 
#keep pregnancy outcome and vitamin D
#geoID as participant ID
keanuAnnotate <- hotinHere |>  
  distinct(geoID, preg_preeclampsia, vitData) |>
  column_to_rownames("geoID")

#match annotation rows to participant columns 
#in the matrix
keanuAnnotate <- keanuAnnotate[colnames(keanuReeves), ]

#load pheatmap
library(pheatmap)

#rename annotation columns for nicer legend
colnames(keanuAnnotate) <- c("Pregnancy Outcome", "Vitamin D Status")

#create annotation colors for pregnancy outcome
#and vitamin D status
keanuColors <- list( 
  "Pregnancy Outcome" = c(
    "Normal" = "#4DAF4A",
    "Preeclampsia" = "#E76F51"
  ), 
  "Vitamin D Status" = c( 
    "Insufficient" = "#45789D",
    "Sufficient" = "#E9C46A"
    )
  )

#create heatmap using expression matrix
pheatmap(
  keanuReeves, 
  #standardized expression within each gene
  #with z scores
  scale = "row",
  #cluster genes and individuals based on expression
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE, 
  #add the two annotation bars 
  annotation_col = keanuAnnotate,
  annotation_colors = keanuColors,
  #use blue for lower and red for higher expression
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#3B4CC0", "#FFFFFF", "#B40426"))(100), 
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  border_color = NA, 
  fontsize_row = 11,
  fontsize = 10,
  cellheight = 25, 
  treeheight_col = 30,
  treeheight_row = 35, 
  #italicize gene names and fix spacing
  labels_row = parse(text = paste0("italic('", rownames(keanuReeves), "')"))
)
```

## Final Submission: alluvial plot

```{r}
#count participants in each combo of 
#vitamin D status and pregnancy outcome
#to figure out size of flow
superAlluvial <- covarData |>  
  count(vitData, preg_preeclampsia)

#superAlluvial

#load the package
library(ggalluvial)

#compare vitamin D status with pregnancy
#outcome. Axis1 = vitamin D status
#and axis2 = pregnancy outcome. 
#number of individuals responsible for width 
#of each flow
ggplot(superAlluvial,
       aes(axis1 = vitData,
           axis2 = preg_preeclampsia,
           y = n)) +
  #flows connecting the categorical variables
  #color by vitamin D status
  geom_alluvium(
    aes(fill = vitData), 
    width = 0.15, 
    alpha = 0.65
    ) +
  #add white boxes to represent each group
  geom_stratum(
    width = 0.15,
    fill = "white", 
    color = "black"
    ) + 
  #label each group inside the box
  geom_text(
    stat = "stratum", 
    aes(label = after_stat(stratum)),
    size = 4
    ) +
  #blue for insufficient and red for sufficient
  #vitamin D, per usual
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
     "Insufficient" = "#377EB8",
     "Sufficient" = "#E41A1C"
    )
  ) +
  #label the axes and fix spacing 
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("Vitamin D Status", "Pregnancy Outcome"),
    expand = c(0.15, 0.05)
  ) +
  #label participant count and vitamin D color
  #legend
  labs(
  x = NULL, 
  y = "Number of Participants",
  fill = "Vitamin D Status"
  ) +
  theme_classic() + 
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
      axis.title = element_text(color = "black"),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
```
